evidence.claim: The identity record marks this device New for the account. 83% of cleared alarms had a New device against 18% of confirmed fraud: on its own a new device is the signature of a cardholder who has just bought a phone, not of a compromise

$128.33 is 4.8x this card's median and above its 95th percentile. Counter-intuitively this is mildly exculpatory: large outliers appear on 16% of cleared alarms and 6% of confirmed fraud, because confirmed fraud tends to stay inside the cardholder's normal range to avoid attention
The bank has 3 confirmed-fraud case(s) already closed on this card (CC-3778, CC-2121, CC-1736), pattern(s): card_not_present_fraud
The cardholder contacted the bank stating they did not make this purchase

Connected components place this card in the graph's giant device-sharing component (2,500 cards). Transitive device sharing percolates at every threshold tested, so membership is not evidence of a ring and carries no weight here; it is recorded because policy R6 asks for the shared element to be named.

Known fraud pattern 3: Card-not-present fraud from a new device: Card-not-present fraud from a new device. Same as above, with the identity record marking the device as `New` for this account, sometimes behind a proxy. Stronger than pattern 2, still not proof: people buy new phones.
